newsitem.title: UK: Chiroscience to give May 30 technical update.
newsitem.headline: Chiroscience to give May 30 technical update.

text.p: Chiroscience Group Plc chief executive John Padfield said on Monday that the company would present a technology and research update to analysts and investors in London on May 30.

In a telephone interview with Reuters he said a similar presentation, which will include a detailed update on progress of Chiroscience's acquisition of the U.S. gene company Darwin Molecular, would be given in New York on June 2.
"The integration with Darwin is going very well," said Padfield, adding that efforts at the Seattle-based company would be targeted on a number of key areas.

He said these included targeting the bone-wasting disease osteoporosis. Darwin was examining "an aspect of bone disease which may be different to conventional approaches to osteoporosis," Padfield said.
Other work at Darwin, which was bought by Chiroscience last December, would concentrate on early-stage psoriasis and a rheumatoid arthritis programme, he added.
The Seattle-based concern would also be able to assist in finding targets for Chiroscience's work on MMP inhibitors, a class of drug which inhibits key enzymes that allow cancer to spread.
Padfield said there was evidence that "different MMPs (enzymes) are raised in different cancers".
Darwin would help to uncover these differences while Chiroscience's scientists in the UK would use their chemistry skills to develop more selective drugs, he added.
